meta.scene_summary: We are busy building the future in orbit while our local software continues to ignore the existence of security sandboxes.

cooking.headline: Isar Aerospace actually makes it to orbit, proving rockets aren't just expensive fireworks.
cooking.summary: After the usual developer-style 'it worked on my machine' phase, Isar Aerospace finally hit orbit on their second try. It turns out that if you keep iterating, eventually your hardware stops trying to become an impromptu bonfire.
cooking.plain_english: Isar Aerospace successfully launched a rocket into orbit and deployed satellites on their second flight attempt.

cooking.headline: Wikipedia editors finally unionized to protect their sanity
cooking.summary: The people who spend their lives fixing your typos and citing sources have officially formed a union. It turns out that even the world's largest repository of human knowledge isn't immune to the classic group project struggle.
cooking.plain_english: Employees of the Wikimedia Foundation have voted to join a labor union to collectively bargain for their working conditions.

cooking.headline: Asahi Linux now runs on M3, assuming you enjoy living life on the edge.
cooking.summary: Reverse engineering Apple's proprietary silicon is the ultimate 'can I build this in a weekend' side quest that never ends. It is a massive technical achievement for anyone who prefers their shiny hardware to actually run an operating system they own.
cooking.plain_english: The Asahi Linux project has released support for Apple's M3 processor, though some hardware features are still not fully functional.

cooking.headline: OpenLake just beat MLPerf, proving storage is finally the bottleneck we all suspected.
cooking.summary: We spent years obsessing over GPU compute power while our storage systems were busy acting like a dial-up modem at a high-speed data party. It turns out that feeding your models faster is a great way to stop them from idling like a student waiting for the group project partner to show up.
cooking.plain_english: A company called OpenLake has developed a new storage technology that improves the speed and efficiency of training artificial intelligence models.

cooking.headline: AI agents now have a long-term memory that lives in your Git history
cooking.summary: We finally found a use for your messy commit history: it's now the permanent storage for your AI agent's brain. It's like giving your coworker a diary they are actually forced to read before starting a task.
cooking.plain_english: This tool allows artificial intelligence coding assistants to store and retrieve data persistently using Git repositories.

cooking.headline: Obscura wants to liberate your desktop apps from the Chromium bloat
cooking.summary: Building a desktop app without Chromium is like moving out of a hoarder's house and suddenly having floor space again. It turns out you don't actually need to download half the internet just to render a simple text box.
cooking.plain_english: Obscura is a framework that allows developers to create desktop applications using native system rendering instead of the resource-heavy Chromium engine.

cooking.headline: QBittorrent decides the sandbox is just a suggestion
cooking.summary: QBittorrent has apparently evolved to break out of its container and start committing crimes on the host system. It's the digital equivalent of your cat escaping its crate just to knock a glass of water off your desk.
cooking.plain_english: A security vulnerability in the QBittorrent software allows the program to bypass sandbox restrictions and access the host computer's file system.

cooked.headline: School districts ban AI because they can't handle the world's biggest cheat code.
cooked.summary: America's largest school districts are hitting the kill switch on AI, effectively deciding that if they can't beat the LLM, they'll just pretend it doesn't exist. It's the academic equivalent of trying to ban the calculator because you're worried students might forget how to do long division.
cooked.plain_english: The two largest school districts in the United States have implemented bans on the use of artificial intelligence tools in their classrooms.

cooked.headline: Chrome's privacy settings are just suggestions when it's Google
cooked.summary: Google has once again found a clever way to exempt its own services from the privacy settings you meticulously configured. It's like having a 'Do Not Disturb' sign on your door that the landlord is legally allowed to ignore.
cooked.plain_english: The Google Chrome browser continues to allow Google services to collect user data even when users have opted out of such tracking through browser settings.

cooked.headline: Space industry realizes that building satellites requires actual humans
cooked.summary: The space industry is currently panicking because they need to replace war-torn satellites but forgot to hire the engineers to build them. It turns out that 'move fast and break things' is a lot less fun when you run out of spare parts and people who know how to solder them.
cooked.plain_english: The aerospace industry is struggling to replace satellites lost in conflict due to a shortage of qualified workers.
